page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that this instance delivers modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests show weak results, with read-only large block transfers reaching 25.86 GB/sec and write operations at 21.97 GB/sec. Geekbench scores align with this trend, placing single-core performance in the bottom 10% and multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, also register in the lower performance tiers.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a qualitative cost advantage for workloads requiring higher memory capacities without the need for high-performance compute resources. Because it relies on older Intel Xeon architecture, it trades off raw processing speed and modern instruction sets, lacking AVX-512 and AMX support, for a more accessible entry point to larger memory allocations.

This instance is suited for memory-bound workloads that do not demand intensive CPU throughput. Appropriate use cases include small-scale databases, caching layers, basic text and image processing, and lightweight web serving. It is less suitable for high-performance computing, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy compilation tasks.
